rows.citation: Damart TPL, Jaquier A, Mandge D, et al. (2024). BluePyEModel (version 1.0.17). Zenodo.
rows.model_type: Detailed conductance-based neuron e-models built from patch-clamp data; NEURON simulator only (per README); not NeuroML-native
rows.controlled_mutations: no - pipeline covers feature extraction, parameter optimisation, validation, plotting and export; no seeded faults or mutant generation described.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - e-features come from several protocols (e.g. IV steps, sAHP in the L5PC example), with separate optimisation and validation protocol lists.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - builds on eFEL/BluePyEfe; models scored by per-feature z-scores against experimental targets.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - model parameters are optimised; which protocols to use for optimisation or validation is specified by hand in a recipe config.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - validation step runs protocols unseen during optimisation with a z-score threshold; held-out stimuli only, not held-out models or fault families.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-assisted editing or transformation of models.
rows.software: BluePyEModel https://github.com/openbraininstitute/BluePyEModel (active; BlueBrain/BluePyEModel archived per GitHub API); PyPI bluepyemodel 1.0.47, Apache-2.0 (examples CC-BY-NC-SA per LICENSE.txt)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: BluePyEModel validates fitted models against experimental feature targets on hand-chosen held-out protocols. NeuroSem would compare a model with its own edited version, not with data: refinement-calibrated tolerances, seeded single-fault mutants, data-driven protocol selection, and held-out models and mutation families. Its validation-protocol split is a useful precedent, and its e-feature scoring could serve as a reference design.
rows.verification_method: DataCite API api.datacite.org/dois/10.5281/zenodo.13685136 (title BluePyEModel, v1.0.17, issued 2024-09-04, 11 creators, Apache-2.0, supplement to BlueBrain/BluePyEModel tree 1.0.17; Zenodo records API returned 504); gh api repos (BlueBrain/BluePyEModel archived, openbraininstitute/BluePyEModel active); PyPI JSON bluepyemodel; README.rst, LICENSE.txt, CITATION.cff (current DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19593077 verified via DataCite as v1.0.47) and examples/L5PC/README.rst read.
rows.found_via: WebSearch BluePyEModel query (DOI from a doi.org result URL; not resolved separately)

rows.citation: Sinha A, Gleeson P, Pandey A, et al. (2026). NeuroML/pyNeuroML: v1.3.22. Zenodo.
rows.model_type: General NeuroML v2 / LEMS models (cells, channels, networks); wraps jNeuroML and other simulator backends
rows.controlled_mutations: no - reads, writes, validates, simulates, converts and analyses NeuroML/LEMS; no mutation or fault-seeding facility found in README or package listing.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - analysis helper sweeps a range of injected current amplitudes to build F-I and I-V curves; no multi-type protocol battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - F-I curve helper uses a spike threshold for firing rates; separate spike-time-versus-dt helper; tuning via Neurotune/pyelectro.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - tuning module fits model parameters; no stimulus protocol selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - general-purpose toolkit; no evaluation design.
rows.software: pyNeuroML https://github.com/NeuroML/pyNeuroML (PyPI pyNeuroML 1.3.22, LGPL-3.0-only per PyPI; LGPL-3.0 per GitHub API; LICENSE.lesser is GNU LGPL v3)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Infrastructure NeuroSem would reuse for validation, jNeuroML simulation and F-I sweeps. Its analyse_spiketime_vs_dt helper already compares spike times across time steps. NeuroSem would add refinement-calibrated per-feature tolerances, a mutation engine, multi-protocol fingerprints and held-out battery selection.
rows.verification_method: PyPI JSON pypi.org/pypi/pyNeuroML/json (1.3.22, uploaded 2026-06-02, first upload 2015-07-27); gh api repos/NeuroML/pyNeuroML (created 2014-12-10, LGPL-3.0) and latest release v1.3.22; README.md, LICENSE.lesser and pyneuroml/analysis/__init__.py (generate_current_vs_frequency_curve, analyse_spiketime_vs_dt) read; DataCite api.datacite.org/dois/10.5281/zenodo.5744044 (README badge DOI; resolved to v1.3.22 record, 2026, lgpl-3.0).
rows.found_via: PyPI JSON https://pypi.org/pypi/pyNeuroML/json; also GitHub search 'pyneuroml' + /repos metadata (duplicate candidate merged into this row)

rows.citation: Ranjan R, Van Geit W, Moor R, et al. (2026). eFEL (version 5.7.34). Zenodo.
rows.model_type: Model-agnostic feature extraction from voltage traces (in vitro recordings or simulations)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - extracts features from user-supplied traces; no model modification.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - the library processes traces with user-given stimulus windows; it defines no stimulation protocols itself.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - standardized definitions for over 90 features (e.g. AP amplitude and width), C++ core with Python interface.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no protocol design or selection.
rows.software: eFEL https://github.com/openbraininstitute/eFEL (active; BlueBrain/eFEL archived per GitHub API); PyPI efel 5.7.34, LGPLv3 (LICENSE.txt: LGPL v3 or later; examples and tests BSD)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Feature-extraction component NeuroSem would reuse, not a competing method. NeuroSem would freeze an eFEL version and its settings, handle undefined features explicitly, and add everything above feature extraction: protocols, tolerances, mutants and battery selection.
rows.verification_method: PyPI JSON pypi.org/pypi/efel/json (5.7.34, uploaded 2026-08-25, license LGPLv3, homepage openbraininstitute/eFEL); gh api repos (openbraininstitute/eFEL active, BlueBrain/eFEL archived) and releases/latest 5.7.34; README.md and LICENSE.txt read; DataCite for zenodo 19604220 (v5.7.34, 2026), 14222078 (v5.7.13, 2024) and 8288734 (v5.0.5, 2023), all LGPL-3.0; README's preferred paper citation verified via Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1093/bioinformatics/btag328 (Mandge D, Tuncel A, Jaquier A, et al. 2026, Bioinformatics 42(6) btag328; abstract read).
rows.found_via: PyPI JSON https://pypi.org/pypi/efel/json; WebSearch results (GitHub BlueBrain/eFEL and openbraininstitute/eFEL; Zenodo records 8288734 and 14222078)

rows.citation: Druckmann S, Banitt Y, Gidon A, et al. (2007). A novel multiple objective optimization framework for constraining conductance-based neuron models by experimental data. Frontiers in Neuroscience.
rows.model_type: Conductance-based compartmental cortical interneuron models (accommodating and fast-spiking); 10 channel conductances among 12 fitted parameters
rows.controlled_mutations: no - fits parameters to experimental recordings with a genetic algorithm; no seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - responses to suprathreshold depolarizing 2 s step currents; discussion names ramps and oscillatory input as future extensions.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - six features (spike rate, accommodation index, first-spike latency, AP overshoot, AHP depth, AP width), errors scaled by experimental SD.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - not performed; discussion raises finding an optimal stimulus or minimal stimulus set as an open question.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - full-text keyword scan found no held-out stimulus or model test; generalizing to unused stimuli is future work.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Source of feature-wise, variability-scaled comparison for fitting to experimental data. NeuroSem would compare original and transformed models with tolerances set by numerical refinement rather than experimental SD. It would also carry out the minimal-stimulus-set selection this paper only raises, and evaluate it on held-out models and mutation families.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.3389/neuro.01.1.1.001.2007 (title, Frontiers in Neuroscience 1(1):7-18, 2007-11-01; lists only Druckmann S). The full 6-author list comes from PubMed E-utilities esummary PMID 18982116 and Europe PMC (PMC2570085, same DOI, title and pages), so the incomplete Crossref deposit does not conflict. Europe PMC abstract and fullTextXML keyword scan read.
rows.found_via: Crossref title query; verified via Crossref + Europe PMC abstract

rows.citation: Druckmann S, Berger TK, Hill S, et al. (2008). Evaluating automated parameter constraining procedures of neuron models by experimental and surrogate data. Biological Cybernetics.
rows.model_type: Conductance-based compartmental neuron models; parameter-fitting methodology
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - surrogate traces come from a model with known parameters and fitting must recover them; this is known ground truth, not fault seeding for detection.
rows.multiple_stimuli: unclear - abstract mentions step current pulses; full text paywalled, so the number and type of protocols is unverified.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - compares feature-based distance functions (first-spike time, spike width, spike frequency) with whole-trace targets.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - contrasts surrogate with experimental targets; abstract reports no held-out model, stimulus or fault-family evaluation.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shows that model-to-model comparisons with known ground truth can make fitting procedures look better than they are, and supports feature-based distances. NeuroSem asks whether a transformation changed behaviour, not whether fitting recovers parameters. It would add single-fault mutants, refinement tolerances, battery selection and held-out generalization. The paper is a useful caution about overinterpreting surrogate results.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1007/s00422-008-0269-2 (6 authors, Biological Cybernetics 99(4-5):371-379, 2008-11); PubMed esummary PMID 19011925 and Europe PMC (matching authors, abstract read); Springer landing page citation meta tags via doi.org (title, vol 99, pages 371-379). Full text not accessible (no PMC).
rows.found_via: Crossref related hit; verified via Crossref + Europe PMC abstract
